title: {{NAME}} and the Silver Striker
moral: Every team is better when everyone brings their true self to the game.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a silver and teal soccer jersey, dark shorts, and teal boots with silver laces — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
The unicorn arrived during pre-season training and stood at the side of the pitch watching with an expression of focused evaluation.

{{NAME}} was practising crosses. His crosses were accurate but lacked pace.

After the tenth cross, the unicorn walked onto the pitch, positioned itself in the striker's area, and the next time {{NAME}} crossed, it headed the ball perfectly into the goal with its horn.

The arc of the ball off the horn: a velocity and curve that was physically extraordinary.

"I wasn't expecting that," said {{NAME}}.

The unicorn looked at him: obviously.

pages.content:
Her name, as best he could translate, was something like first light. He called her Lumen.

Lumen's horn gave the ball a specific spin when she headed it: a spiral trajectory that was almost impossible to read for goalkeepers because the ball moved in three planes simultaneously.

He could reproduce a version of it with his instep, but Lumen's version was four times more effective.

He designed training sessions around their partnership: his crosses, her finishes, with a Stegosaurus that had arrived during a temporal event standing in goal because it was available and surprisingly reflexive.

pages.content:
The matches that season were unlike any {{NAME}} had played.

Lumen played in the final third, and opponents simply had no defensive framework for a unicorn striker: no precedent, no training, no rulebook that addressed it directly.

But what made the partnership extraordinary wasn't the novelty. It was the communication.

Lumen would touch her horn briefly to {{NAME}}'s shoulder before each match. In that second, he understood exactly what she was going to do in the first ten minutes.

He shaped his play around it. They were unstoppable.

pages.content:
The championship final: a team that had scouted them extensively and had a defensive plan specifically for Lumen.

They double-marked her all game. She touched {{NAME}}'s shoulder before kick-off and showed him the image: use the space they leave.

With two defenders following Lumen everywhere, {{NAME}} and his other teammates had unprecedented space.

Four goals. Two from Lumen breaking the mark at the right moment. Two from {{NAME}} exploiting the space she created.

Champions.

pages.content:
After the season, the temporal displacement resolved and Lumen needed to return to her own era.

{{NAME}} stood at the portal with her.

"Next season," he said.

She touched her horn to his hand: a specific pulse he had come to understand meant something more than yes. Something closer to: always.

She went through.

He walked home carrying the memory of the horn's touch, and in his room that night he picked up his football and held it and thought about the spin she gave it.

He could still feel it. He always would.
